shared_text:
The flight. A wide-body airliner departing from an airport in the early hours of the morning. Visual conditions, with wind.

The crew. The first officer was the pilot flying for the take-off and the captain the pilot monitoring. The captain taxied and lined up the aircraft. A relief first officer was also on the flight deck.

What happened. The crew had completed the before-take-off checklist and runway verification. The captain noted several aircraft on final. The taxiway from the holding point joins the runway in a curve. As a landing aircraft crossed the threshold, the tower controller cleared this aircraft to line up and wait. The landing aircraft reported that it had passed its planned exit, and the controller told it to expedite to the next one. The controller then cleared this aircraft for an immediate take-off. It was still taxiing into position, in a slight right turn onto the centreline. The captain centred the nose on the centreline while continuing to roll forward, as usual, and believed the line-up was complete. The captain asked whether everyone was ready, handed control to the first officer, set 55 per cent thrust and, when stable, selected take-off thrust. The main gear trucks had not yet locked into position after the turn. A take-off configuration warning sounded, with a main gear steering message. At about 10 knots the captain rejected the take-off and took control. The first officer told the tower that they had rejected the take-off on the runway.
safe_outcome: The tower controller instructed the aircraft now on short final to go around. The crew taxied along the runway, left it at a later exit and told the tower that no assistance was needed. They completed the checklists, checked brake cooling and minimum fuel, and later made a normal take-off. No one was hurt and no aircraft was damaged.
bad_outcome: The landing aircraft's crew saw the conflict late and went around from about 50 feet, passing low over this aircraft. A flight attendant on the landing aircraft was thrown off balance by the abrupt go-around and received a minor injury.
notes: Variant B-landing: this aircraft was the one departing; the conflicting traffic was the aircraft on short final, which ATC sent around. Bracket 'this aircraft': after the low-speed reject the aircraft was on the runway. Removed under rule 3: both Cause sections ('distractions and rushing'; the immediate take-off instruction 'was a factor'), both Suggestions (runway priority once assigned; straightening the aircraft before TOGA; 'one more second of line up'), the captain's praise of the other two pilots, and the captain's surprise at the warning (the contemporaneous belief that the line-up was complete is kept). Moved to the safe ending under rule 5: ATC sending the short-final traffic around, the taxi clear, brake-cooling and fuel checks, and the later normal take-off. Dropped as post-event follow-up: the calls to dispatch, operations and the supervisor. Removed under rule 6: airport, runway and taxiway names. Judgement calls: the first officer's Suggestions line that the crew 'felt the need/desire' to help the tower clear the landing traffic is a motive, but it is framed as the outcome of the crew's later discussion, so it was treated as reflection and left out. The gear trucks not having locked is stated plainly as a fact established afterwards (first officer's account). Crew size is coded 2, but the captain's narrative names a relief first officer and asks 'the crew' if everyone was ready, so the relief pilot is included. Dropped for length: the restated take-off clearance, the tower's stated reason for hurrying the landing aircraft ('for landing traffic as well as us'), and 'all engines running for short taxi'. Reject speed given as 'less than 20 kts (estimate 10 kts)'; rendered as 'about 10 knots'.
